comment: Licence decisions that the build cannot derive by itself (ADR 0003, ADR 0009). tools/package.ps1
derives the shipped components from the audited layout and uses this file only for elections,
required credit lines, licence texts missing from vcpkg's copyright files, and ports that must never
ship. Each entry names the port version it was reviewed for: packaging fails when the build ships
another version, so a dependency upgrade is reviewed here (and in docs/legal/third-party-notices.md).
"assets" names the bundled data assets (assets/<id>) that are third-party data under their own terms:
their licence text (a file of the verified asset) goes to licenses/<id>, their credit lines to
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, and the SBOM gives their files that licence (ADR 0023). Every other bundled
asset is Lucent's own (MIT). Lucent's logo (assets/branding), built into the programs and Setup and
never installed as a file, is not covered by the MIT License: packaging takes its terms from
assets/branding/provenance.json for THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and the SBOM (ADR 0025).
"distribution" records how Lucent is distributed (ADR 0024): packaging refuses a commercial distribution
built with a non-commercial Inno Setup compiler, and builds the corresponding-source package the
provision names. A port marked "lgpl" (or "correspondingSource", for another copyleft licence) has its
upstream source archives, vcpkg recipe and build record in Lucent-<version>-corresponding-source.zip;
packaging fails when a shipped port's licence leaves no choice but a copyleft licence and its entry
marks neither, or when a marked port is missing from the archive. A LicenseRef- alternative (a vendor's
commercial licence) or an unknown identifier is no choice Lucent can take: "concluded" records an
election. GPL or AGPL code without an exception fails packaging even when marked, unless the entry's
"strongCopyleftAdr" names the ADR that accepted it (ADR 0003); copyleft code compiled into the programs
(a header-only port) fails too, a file-level copyleft (MPL, EPL, CDDL) unless "fileLevelCopyleftReview"
records its review (W12 review LIC-4). The patches a marked port's recipe applies are listed with their
files and dates in LGPL-NOTICE.txt and the archive (W12 review LIC-1); a port's "comment", which
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt repeats, must name every patch that changes more than build files. Since the W12
gate-8 reading of 2026-10-16: "declared" records what a library's authors offer it under where the port's
declaration falls short; "parts" names the parts of a library under their own licences, whose terms
packaging takes verbatim from the verified source archive (the member, from the line holding "first" to
the next holding "last") into licenses/<port>/<as>, with "terms" when the archive names a licence without
its text; a part compiled into the shipped files ("compiled" not false) must have its licence in
"concluded". "lucentAssets" names Lucent's own bundled assets (MIT) for THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt's Data list.
Since the gate-8 review, round 1 (2026-10-16): a part may give its own "version", the "source" archive that holds it
(a port built from several), "lastWhole" (the last line is the one whose trimmed text is "last"), and its licence's text
as "text" (a member of the same archive, whole or from "first" to "last", with "about" when the excerpt is not the
licence's whole text) or "textIn" (licence files other components ship, each with a marker line that must be in it
and "holds", what the file holds); its licence may carry an exception ("X WITH Y"). The
third-party code Qt's own SBOM records inside a Qt component's shipped files must be covered by its "concluded" (an
election for a choice) unless "attributionsNotCompiled" names it with the reason this build does not compile it. A
recipe's own scripts that change the library's files before the build are named in "scriptedEdits" (script, changes),
listed with the patches. "libraryLicence" is the licence of a library's own code, without its parts and third-party
code (part of "concluded"): the licence of the lines its recipe's patches quote, for the SBOM's recipe files.
"toolchainLibraries" records the code of the compiler's own libraries inside Lucent's
programs (the C++ standard library of the reviewed MSVC toolset), its parts' notices pinned by the SHA-256 of the
headers that hold them; "distribution.installerTool" pins the licence file of the reviewed Inno Setup version.
Since the gate-8 review, round 2 (2026-10-16): a part's licence text comes from a verified source only ("text" or
"textIn"; "terms" is refused). "fileLicences" gives the licence of a file a patch changes that states none in an SPDX
line (files, licence or NOASSERTION, the statement of the file or the evidence of the archive that shows it, comment);
every patch's SBOM licence is MIT and the licences of the files it changes. "attributionLicences" corrects the licence
Qt's SBOM records for code inside Qt (qtSbom, licence, evidence, texts), "attributionNotices" takes its NOTICE lines,
"attributionSources" names the Source Code Form of copyleft code at the commit Qt's SBOM records. A toolchain library
with "kit": "windows-sdk" is code of the Windows SDK in shipped binaries (C++/WinRT), its licence pinned by SHA-256 and
every binary probed. "thirdPartySources" pins by git blob id the files of published sources kept in installer\third-party
(packaging never downloads). "distribution.installerTool.parts" names the code of others inside Inno Setup with its
licence and, under a copyleft licence, its source; "distribution.correspondingSource.licenceTexts" adds licence texts
the archive's files need. "vcRedistributable.reviewed" names the terms of the reviewed redistributable, and
"termsReview" records the owner's review of the conditions under which Lucent redistributes it.

signing.comment: Release installers are unsigned until a code-signing certificate exists; the signing pipeline (LUCENT_SIGN_CERT_SHA1, ADR 0009 decision 13) stays ready. An unsigned package cannot be published on an update channel (New-LucentReleaseManifest), so unsigned releases are built with -UpdateChannel none. Set release to "signed" in the release commit that introduces signing: packaging then refuses a Setup without a release signature.

qtbase.comment: Qt modules are used under LGPL-3.0-only, dynamically linked (ADR 0003, decision 3). Qt compiles third-party code into the shipped files, which Qt's own SBOM records and the list below names; the licence covers each (the W12 gate-8 review, round 1), with Lucent's elections: FTL for the anti-aliasing rasterizer from FreeType 2 (FTL OR GPL-2.0-only), CC0-1.0 for BLAKE2 (CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0). The Vulkan Memory Allocator, which Qt's SBOM also records for Qt6Gui.dll, is not compiled in this build (Vulkan is off). Qt's bundled copies of zlib, PCRE2, FreeType, HarfBuzz, libjpeg, libpng, MD4C and double-conversion are not compiled: this build uses the system libraries, which ship as their own components; nor are its Unix, Apple, Android, WebAssembly, Wayland and X11 code, its D-Bus and SQL modules (off), or Qt Test, which does not ship. Qt's CMake build files are BSD-3-Clause. vcpkg's recipe patches Qt's source with 26 patches (W12 review LIC-1; their summary corrected by the W12 gate-8 reading of 2026-10-16). 18 change only CMake build files (use-shared-mime-info.patch applies only with a feature Lucent does not use). md4c.diff changes src/gui/text/qtextmarkdownimporter.cpp, in Qt6Gui.dll (it removes a compile-time assertion). silence-winrtbase-coroutine-warnings.diff adds a #define that silences a deprecation warning to src/corelib/platform/windows/qt_winrtbase_p.h, which Qt compiles where it uses C++/WinRT (configured in this build), and to its configure test. clang-cl_source_location.patch, clang-cl_QGADGET_fix.diff and QTBUG-145703.patch change headers in ways that take effect only with clang-cl or in static builds. use_inotify_on_freebsd.patch changes a condition for FreeBSD in src/corelib/io/qfilesystemwatcher.cpp; macdeployqt-symlinks.patch changes the macOS deployment tool macdeployqt (src/tools/macdeployqt/shared/shared.cpp), which is not built on Windows; windeployqt-webengine-debug-resources.patch changes the deployment tool windeployqt (src/tools/windeployqt/main.cpp), which Lucent's build runs but does not ship. Every patch is listed with its files and the registry commit's date in LGPL-NOTICE.txt and the corresponding-source archive; each patch's licence is that of the files it changes (the SBOM: macdeployqt-symlinks.patch and windeployqt-webengine-debug-resources.patch quote files under GPL-3.0-only with the Qt GPL exception, the commercial alternative being none Lucent holds). The third-party code compiled into the shipped Qt files is listed with its holders and licences from Qt's own SBOM; the licence texts are sections of the port's copyright file. Where Qt's SBOM falls short, the gate-8 review, round 2, corrects it: Khronos' OpenGL headers are MIT-Khronos-old (Qt's REUSE.toml), Apache Tika's MIME type definitions include PRONOM's under the Open Government Licence 3.0 and come with the lines of Tika's NOTICE that pertain to them, and the Public Suffix List's Source Code Form is public_suffix_list.dat at the commit Qt's SBOM records. The same review found code of the Windows SDK compiled into the Qt files: C++/WinRT (MIT), which Qt's build configures (QT_FEATURE_cpp_winrt), in Qt6Core.dll and qwindows.dll (toolchainLibraries.cppwinrt); Qt6Gui.dll's Direct3D 12 backend includes the SDK's d3d12.h and d3d12sdklayers.h (MIT) and dxcapi.h (University of Illinois/NCSA), which give it declarations and GUID constants only, no code, as the C++ library's thread headers do for Lucent's programs.

libraw.comment: LibRaw is offered under LGPL-2.1-only or CDDL-1.0; Lucent elects LGPL-2.1-only (ADR 0003, decision 2). Its COPYRIGHT names parts under their own licences, listed below with their notices from LibRaw's source archive (the W12 gate-8 reading of 2026-10-16): the DCB demosaic and FBDD denoise code (BSD-3-Clause) and code from the Adobe DNG SDK 1.4 (MIT; the archive names the licence without its text, so since the gate-8 review, round 2, the part's file points to the MIT texts that ship as nlohmann-json's licence files), both in raw_r.dll, and the X3F tools (BSD-3-Clause), which the port does not compile. vcpkg's port declares 'BSD-3-Clause AND (LGPL-2.1-only OR CDDL-1.0)', which leaves out the MIT code. LibRaw uses code from Dave Coffin's dcraw.c but, its COPYRIGHT says, none of its RESTRICTED code. Its Sony YCC and lossless JPEG decoders (src/decoders/sonycc.cpp, src/decompressors/losslessjpeg.cpp, internal/losslessjpeg.h, in raw_r.dll) are 'partially backported from DNGLab's rust code' (DNGLab, by Daniel Vogelbacher), as their headers say, under LibRaw's choice of LGPL-2.1 or CDDL-1.0; LibRaw's archive states no licence of DNGLab, whose repository states LGPL-2.1 (read for the gate-8 review, round 2), so Lucent's election of LGPL-2.1 fits it, while whether CDDL-1.0 is available for these files depends on DNGLab's licence. Its optional modules are not compiled (the port defines only USE_JPEG, USE_JPEG8, USE_LCMS2 and USE_ZLIB): the RawSpeed glue with RawSpeed's camera data (RawSpeed/rawspeed_xmldata.cpp, CC BY-SA 3.0, compiled only with USE_RAWSPEED), the Adobe DNG SDK, the GoPro GPR SDK and the Raspberry Pi decoder (the W12 gate-8 review, round 1). The port builds LibRaw with LibRaw-cmake's build files (its second archive): its CMakeLists.txt is GPL-2.0-or-later (Gilles Caulier's notice), its cmake/ files KDE's BSD scripts and files without a notice, which its BSD-3-Clause LICENSE covers; none of it is compiled except libraw_config.h, which LibRaw LLC's template cmake/data/libraw_config.h.cmake makes (LibRaw's own licence). vcpkg's dependencies.patch and fix-install.patch change those build files (CMakeLists.txt and cmake/), so they are under LibRaw-cmake's licences, not LibRaw's.

lensfun.comment: Lensfun's README licenses its libraries under the GNU LGPL, version 3 (the public header lensfun.h additionally states LGPL-2.0-or-later; the sources of libs/lensfun carry copyright lines without a licence statement), so the library is used under LGPL-3.0-only. Its libs/regex is a subset of the TRE regular expression library (Copyright (c) 2001-2006 Ville Laurikari), whose files carry LGPL-2.1-or-later notices: Lensfun's build compiles it into lensfun.dll as the static library tre_regex where no regex.h exists, as with MSVC (the build log: 'regex.h - not found'; lens.cpp calls regcomp and regexec), so the licence names it, with its notice below (the W12 gate-8 review, round 1; until then this note said the other library sources carry no notice). The port declares no licence and its copyright file is the README's licence section with the GPL-3.0 and LGPL-3.0 texts. Its programs (GPL-3.0) are not built (BUILD_LENSTOOL=OFF) and its Python module is not built; nor is the GNU getopt of libs/getopt (GPL-2.0-or-later), which its build adds only with BUILD_TESTS (off). Its lens database (CC BY-SA 3.0) is not part of the port: Lucent ships the database as the verified asset assets/lens-database with its own licence text (see Data below; ADR 0023). A replaceable DLL (ADR 0003); vcpkg's recipe patches only its CMakeLists.txt (fix_build.patch), listed in LGPL-NOTICE.txt. That top-level CMakeLists.txt carries no licence notice and Lucent's reading of the archive finds no statement that covers it (the gate-8 review, round 2): the README gives the GPL-3.0 to 'the build system (the contents of the build/ subdirectory plus the ac.py file)', which 0.3.4 no longer holds (its ChangeLog: 'Removed old non-CMake build system'), and its other statements name libs/, apps/, the documentation, tests/, tools/ and data/. The SBOM therefore makes no assertion of the patch's licence (NOASSERTION).

glib.comment: GLib is LGPL-2.1-or-later; the port's declared licence adds 'LGPL-2.1-only OR MPL-1.1' for code Lucent does not ship (only glib-2.0-0.dll, which lensfun.dll imports, ships; GObject, GIO, GModule and GThread do not). Built from Lucent's overlay port (cmake/ports/glib, shipped as licenses\glib\recipe), whose source is modified by three patches (W12 review LIC-1): vcpkg's use-libiconv-on-windows.patch (glib/gconvert.c converts with GNU libiconv instead of the bundled win_iconv; meson.build) and libintl.patch (meson.build), and Lucent's lucent-neutral-locale-dir.patch (meson.build), which keeps the build machine's install prefix out of the DLL. Each is listed with its files and date in LGPL-NOTICE.txt and the corresponding-source archive. A replaceable DLL (ADR 0003, ADR 0023). glib-2.0-0.dll also holds the dirent emulation of glib/dirent (mingw-runtime's, placed in the public domain), which has no licence to name, and the gnulib and libcharset copies (LGPL-2.1-or-later). Not compiled for this build (the W12 gate-8 review, round 1): glib/gutilsprivate.c (MIT; only on Unix), glib/valgrind.h (bzip2-style; glib/gvalgrind.h includes it only when the compiler is not MSVC), the bundled win_iconv.c (public domain; use-libiconv-on-windows.patch makes gconvert.c use GNU libiconv) and girepository's CMPH (LGPL-2.1-only OR MPL-1.1; not shipped). Its Unicode tables, generated from the Unicode Character Database, carry no notice of their own.

gettext-libintl.comment: GNU libintl from gettext-runtime (intl/COPYING.LIB), imported by GLib. Built from Lucent's overlay port (cmake/ports/gettext-libintl, shipped as licenses\gettext-libintl\recipe), whose source is modified by three patches (W12 review LIC-1): vcpkg's uwp.patch (gettext-runtime/intl/langprefs.c, gettext-runtime/intl/gnulib-lib/localcharset.c) and 0003-Fix-win-unicode-paths.patch (gettext-runtime/intl/loadmsgcat.c opens catalogs by UTF-8 file names), and Lucent's lucent-no-builder-paths.patch (gettext-runtime/intl/dcigettext.c, gettext-runtime/intl/gnulib-lib/relocatable.c), which keeps the build machine's folders out of the DLL (its default catalog folder and the relocation prefixes Lucent never uses). Each is listed with its files and date in LGPL-NOTICE.txt and the corresponding-source archive. A replaceable DLL (ADR 0023). Its plural-expression parser intl/plural.c was generated by GNU Bison 3.8.2 and holds Bison's parser skeleton, under GPL-3.0-or-later with the Bison exception, which lets the larger work be distributed under its own terms; it is compiled into intl-8.dll (the build log compiles plural.c), so the licence names it, with its notice and the GPL's text below (the W12 gate-8 review, round 1). Besides its patches, the recipe runs vcpkg's bashify.cmake on gettext-runtime/configure before configuring, which rewrites that build script's libtool quoting into bash variable expansion (listed with the patches), and its portfile rewrites the Makefiles the build generates. The build also generates gnulib's alloca.h from gnulib-lib/alloca.in.h, whose notice is GPL-3.0-or-later without an exception (configure finds no alloca.h for MSVC), and gnulib-lib/vasnprintf.c, compiled into intl-8.dll, includes it; for MSVC it gives only '#include <malloc.h>' and '#define alloca _alloca', so no expressive code of it is compiled and the licence names no GPL for it (the gate-8 review, round 2).

vcRedistributable.name: Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64)
vcRedistributable.licenseText: MICROSOFT SOFTWARE LICENSE TERMS - MICROSOFT VISUAL C++ 2015 - 2022 RUNTIME (EULA ID Cpp_2015-2022_ENU.1033): the terms Microsoft's redistributable installer, vc_redist.x64.exe, shows when it is run on its own (its license.rtf). Lucent Setup carries the redistributable unmodified and runs it, only when the computer's runtime is older, silently (/install /quiet /norestart), so its window and these terms are not displayed; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt names them. Lucent redistributes it as Distributable Code under the Microsoft Software License Terms of Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, with which it was installed (https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=2179911; the list of Distributable Code: https://aka.ms/vs/17/redist.txt), whose conditions the project owner reviews (installer\license-policy.json, vcRedistributable.termsReview).

reviewed.licenceName: MICROSOFT SOFTWARE LICENSE TERMS - MICROSOFT VISUAL C++ 2015 - 2022 RUNTIME
reviewed.comment: Read for the gate-8 review, round 2: the English license.rtf (SHA-256 8099dc3cf9502c335da829e5c755948a12e3e6de490eb492a99deb673d883d8b) of the redistributable's own user interface, taken with 7-Zip from this vc_redist.x64.exe (Authenticode-signed by Microsoft, as packaging checks); its first lines name the terms, its last line the EULA ID. Another redistributable stops packaging until its terms are read again.

termsReview.terms: Microsoft Software License Terms of Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, as the installation records them: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=2179911 (state.json of the Visual Studio instance); Distributable Code list: https://aka.ms/vs/17/redist.txt (Licenses\1033\Redist.txt of the installation)
termsReview.covers: the redistribution of vc_redist.x64.exe inside Lucent Setup, which runs it silently, and the static runtime startup code of the MSVC toolset (msvcrt.lib's objects, such as mainCRTStartup and the DLL entry point, Microsoft's own code under these terms) linked into Lucent.exe, lucent-worker.exe and every vcpkg DLL
termsReview.comment: The gate-8 review, round 2, found that the conditions of these terms for Distributable Code were not reviewed (the ledger said 'not reviewed'). The project owner reviews them and records the result here (status 'reviewed', the date and what the conditions require, such as showing or naming Microsoft's terms or running the redistributable with /passive); until then packaging warns and release checklist gate 8 is open.
